nodes.title: director20: 16 lessons (4 pilot topics x steady, stuck, offtopic, steering), Director only, reactive rule-based child, int/r6 52b3ff1cc (integration 36); 1,541 model calls, about $1.06; four Opus judges at high effort, one per topic, counting by hand. Verdicts 256 of 256; 0 contradictions, 0 unsaid boards, 0 misgrades, 0 false keys in all four topics (contradictions 9, 1, 0 over the last three runs). Axes (listening, worked example, class level, screen and speech, register, promises): c4 3, 4, 4, 4, 3.5, 3.5; c5-t01 3, 4, 3.5, 4, 3, 2.5; c5-t02 3, 4, 3.5, 4.5, 3.5, 3; c6 3.5, 4, 3.5, 4.5, 3.5, 3.5. c6 passes every line of the scale gate, the first topic to do so. Of director19's ten faults nine are gone or reduced; 'a give-up with help spent gets no key' is still there on the same three rows. J2: 7 model-written reply sentences, 3 odd or wrong, 2 more replies fell to a neutral joint; 3 of 10 parks never returned to. Not exercised: a second clarify, a child with history, generated games, the third skill. Results in evals/hybrid-side-by-side/results/2026-11-11-director20/.

The dry matrix held 'a give-up with help spent gets the key' at zero while the live lesson said the point again on the same three rows as director19 (c4 stuck 12, c5-t01 stuck 12, c5-t02 steering 30). In the live path the reply model's text failed a guard and was repaired to a different unit part. The dry predicates check the walk's choice; they do not see what the reply layer finally says. A gate that passes while the fault it names is live is not a gate for that fault.

Rejected: reading the J2 replay's pass rate (76 of 80 clean under the predicate) as evidence that her reply after an aside is good. In director20 the same code produced 7 model sentences of which the judges found 3 odd or wrong, and most first drafts were the next card's text. The predicate measures safe and on the child's word; it cannot measure whether a sentence answers what the child said. A sentence a child hears is judged by a reader or it is authored.

After director20: (R1) her reply after an aside is authored, not model-written: per kind of aside, three return questions and three reply forms with one slot for a word of the child's, judged by a reader before use; the model path and its predicate leave lessons (the pre-set clause fired: 3 of 7 odd). (G3) The dry predicates also run over every live run's rows, and a live run with a predicate above zero is not sent to judges; authored cells (key and why, point, simpler, remediation, joint) are said as written by code and a repair may never swap one unit part for another. (P1) Every park is queued and returned to before the goodbye, in a turn of its own; she asks no question whose answer her next turn ignores. (L1 to L4) New cells: a give-up at a check-in gets the simpler then the card; a clarify after a key gets the why reworded; a clarify at the greeting gets one plain line then the hook; a Hindi request says the part's simpler in Hindi. (S1) After a hint she re-asks only the card's question; an older card gets an authored lead-in. (W1) Code no longer swaps words inside authored sentences; one term per idea per language form is fixed in the script. The staged 30 stay held. Reverse if: the judged library reads worse than director20's model replies (then the model writes with the library as examples); or code-said cells make register fall in two or more topics (then the model may join parts under a word-for-word predicate); or question-only re-asks prove unclear (then the givens return after a second miss).
